events.label: Walmart (WMT) Q2 2026 earnings — highest-signal consumer read of the week
events.note: Updated Aug 19 night: HD beat (+1.7% comps, Aug 18) and TGT beat (+3.8% comps, Aug 19) but TGT fell on macro override — consumer data transmitted in numbers, not in price. WMT is the third and final data point in the retail gauntlet. Consensus: ~$186.3–186.9B revenue, comparable-store sales ~4%, EPS ~$0.73. Three-of-three beats would define whether UMich 51.0 and retail sales −0.6% reflect survey pessimism or actual spending behavior. BofA, RBC, Deutsche Bank and Oppenheimer have lowered comps forecasts to 2.5–3.5% range; WMT's traffic commentary spans grocery, general merchandise, and pharmacy across income cohorts — the most comprehensive per-income-cohort consumer read of the three. Key signal: comparable-store sales guidance and per-visit spend shift toward or away from lower-margin grocery.

events.label: SPCX next staggered tranche (~7%) — second unlock after Aug 6 first tranche
events.note: Updated Aug 19 night: 30Y fell to 5.196% (from 5.31% prior, Bessent buyback announcement) — improves the rate-compression backdrop vs. the Aug 17 night note. Brent still near $89–90 on Hormuz premium. SPCX absorbed the first tranche at $105–$115 (Aug 6–7); current ~$140 zone. WMT earnings same day — consumer data provides macro context for the lock-up absorption. October Q3 Starlink profitability remains the fundamental anchor. Front-run signal: close below $120 on elevated volume before Aug 20.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — chip sector under multi-week pressure entering print
events.note: Updated Aug 19 night: Chip sector enters the print with AMD at ~$465 (below $484 containment signal), AVGO at ~$362 (below $380 structural support), SOXX down materially over the past week from Netlist DDR5 patent action. 30Y fell to 5.196% (Bessent buyback + FOMC CPI-only framing) — rate relief improved but chips fell through it. Aug 19 demonstrated chips do not recover automatically into rate relief. Bar unchanged: gross margin above 78% AND data-center guide materially above the most aggressive sell-side estimate — both simultaneously required. Jackson Hole begins Aug 27 — no de-risk window between the print and Warsh's keynote.

events.label: Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (Aug 27–29) — Warsh keynote; 30Y at 5.20% after Bessent buyback
events.note: Updated Aug 19 night: FOMC Minutes (Aug 19) confirmed CPI-persistence framing from the three dissenters — the fiscal sustainability concern was secondary. Bessent's doubled buyback operations (effective Sept 9, through Nov 4) pushed 30Y down 9bps to 5.196%. Five consecutive soft data prints (NFP −23K, CPI core 2.5%, PPI flat, retail sales −0.6%, UMich 51.0) argue for patience; Bessent's buyback policy provides supply-side support. Warsh's keynote will establish whether the Fed chair sees the current policy constellation — rate hold + buyback support — as sufficient, or whether additional rate action remains on the table. NVDA earnings land Aug 26 — one day before the keynote. UMich final (Aug 28) is a within-symposium data point.

events.label: AVGO Q3 FY2026 earnings (est.) — through $380 structural support; VMware + AI concentration dual overhang
events.note: Updated Aug 19 night: AVGO fell 5% to ~$362 on August 19, breaking through $380 structural support. VMware CVE-2026-59310 active exploitation (361 IPs, 47 countries per Aug 14 disclosure) + 72% AI revenue concentration (~72% of next-quarter sequential growth) create dual overhang. At ~65x trailing P/E, any miss or margin compression compounds. Q3 FY2026 results (est. September 4–5) are the first public accounting of both: VMware remediation costs in financial guidance, enterprise customer commentary on the incident, and AI revenue breadth. $380 is now resistance; $340–350 is the next structured support zone. Flip: recovery above $380 on volume, or formal VMware incident-containment statement before earnings.

events.label: Bessent Treasury long-dated buyback ops begin — $4B+ per op, 10-20yr and 20-30yr bonds
events.note: Added Aug 19 night: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced August 19 the department will double the size of long-dated bond buyback operations, raising the maximum per-operation from $2B to at least $4B for bonds maturing in the 10-to-20-year and 20-to-30-year ranges. Effective September 9, runs through November 4 (end of current refunding quarter). Immediate market impact: 30Y fell 9bps to 5.196% on the announcement. The program provides structural demand support for the long end through the NVDA print (Aug 26), Jackson Hole (Aug 27–29), and into October. If underlying supply dynamics ($432B July deficit, $1.7T corporate issuance) overwhelm the $4B+ buyback, the 30Y could reassert above 5.25% before the program begins.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
